hypothesis: bf16 output projection and c3 subtraction break common-output-bias invariance and leak gradients into an unidentifiable output direction.

statistics.forward_unit: 60 equally weighted episode means from 352 windows
statistics.gradient_unit: 11 canonical batches of 32 windows; descriptive batch-mean RMS

conclusions: Both checkpoints at all four timesteps satisfy the preregistered forward and backward numerical-mechanism criteria.
Head fp32 plus fp32 rebase reduces bias-perturbation output change and bias-gradient leakage by more than 99% everywhere; casting the already rounded output to fp32 is insufficient.
R3 raw rotation-output RMS is about 2771 versus R2 about 0.575, exposing a large common-offset cancellation regime.
Full-fp32 R3 rotation L1 remains about 2.01-2.05 and significantly exceeds R2; precision correction alone does not recover this trained candidate.
The deterministic first-future-frame constraint remains a separate structural limitation; no native rollout or optimizer update was performed.
next_action: Retain R2+CG. Develop a separate reviewable training proposal that preserves learnable first-frame acceleration and avoids subtracting large unconstrained outputs. Do not restart R3 or promote its weights based on this diagnostic.
